name: NTT DATA / NTT Ltd.
product_focus: Managed SD-WAN, Managed SASE, Palo Alto/Zscaler partnerships
evidence_summary: NTT sources evidence 24x7 managed SD-WAN via global operations centers, portal visibility and managed SASE with Prisma SASE.
cost_model: Quote-based managed service; global design/delivery/support, SD-WAN vendor and security stack determine cost.
key_differentiators: 24x7 managed SD-WAN delivery via global operations centres with strong portal visibility.
Managed SASE partnership with Palo Alto Networks (Prisma SASE) for buyers wanting that platform under managed service.
Strong global delivery footprint including APAC, EMEA and Americas.
best_fit_for: Multinational enterprises wanting truly global managed delivery with consistent operations across regions.
Buyers wanting Prisma SASE consumed as a fully managed service.
Organisations prioritising managed service maturity and global SOC/NOC depth.
watch_outs: Platform fit depends on which vendor is being proposed (Palo Alto, Zscaler, others); evaluate platform independently.
Commercial complexity is meaningful at global scale; ensure scope and RACI are explicit.
DIY/self-managed model is not the primary positioning.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: Predictive analytics within the Managed Network Services platform.

resilience.note: Global Tier 1 IP backbone with multi-vendor managed redundancy.

profile.platform_architecture: NTT DATA combines a global Tier 1 IP backbone with one of the world's largest IT services businesses, delivering managed SD-WAN on a multi-vendor bench (Cisco, VeloCloud, Versa, Fortinet, Palo Alto) across 190+ countries' reach. Data centre, cloud and network services interlock, and Asia-Pacific delivery depth is a standout among global providers.
profile.security_sase: Managed SASE pairs the platform bench with leading SSE stacks under NTT's substantial security division: global SOCs, threat intelligence and consulting at IT-services scale. Predictive analytics within the Managed Network Services platform add operational intelligence. Depth follows the platform; the services organisation behind it is among the largest anywhere.
profile.service_support_channel: Fully managed and co-managed with 24x7 follow-the-sun operations, named service management and consulting-led change delivery. UK presence is significant via NTT DATA UK. Japanese heritage shows in APAC strength and delivery discipline.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-site managed pricing on term, quote based. The Netify verdict: shortlist NTT for global estates with Asia-Pacific weight, change programmes wanting consulting plus network plus security from one group, and buyers consolidating data centre, cloud and WAN relationships. Smaller UK estates will find the machine bigger than they need.

vendor_faqs.a: Asia-Pacific depth is the differentiator, with Japan home advantage and strong delivery across the region, alongside credible Americas and EMEA operations. Global estates with APAC weight shortlist NTT early.

vendor_faqs.q: Does NTT bring security scale to SASE?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes: a global security division with SOCs, threat intelligence and consulting wraps the chosen SSE platform, suiting buyers who want managed security operations rather than just licensed software.

vendor_faqs.q: Is NTT right for mid-market UK companies?
vendor_faqs.a: Usually only when part of a wider NTT relationship or global parent estate; domestically focused mid-market buyers typically fit nimbler UK MSPs or carriers better.

shortlist_summary: NTT deliver managed SD-WAN via a network of global operations centres running 24x7, which means the follow-the-sun support model is genuinely backed up rather than just described in a service document. Typically shortlisted by multinational businesses with complex, multi-region estates where around-the-clock managed operations and strong portal transparency are non-negotiable requirements.
cost_note: Per-site managed on term; premium, consulting-led global delivery.
uk_basis: UK contracting entity (NTT DATA UK) of a Japanese parent, with UK delivery and operations.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: As a fully managed solution, enterprises will be able to conserve scarce IT resources and reduce the complexity of managing a global network and security infrastructure.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: NTT positions its Managed Campus Networks with Prisma SASE offering explicitly as a fully managed solution, and the nttglobal.net SD-WAN pages state NTT can operate the service end to end. Note that the fully managed wording sits on an offering built on Palo Alto Networks technology, so NTT is operating, not authoring, the security layer.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: Customers have the option to self-manage via a web portal or NTT can offer managed services.
f03_co_managed_service.note: The published wording describes an either/or choice (customer self-manages via portal, OR NTT manages) rather than an explicitly shared-responsibility co-managed model. The NTT DATA/Cisco managed SASE brochure describes people-augmented, technology-augmented and hybrid operating models, which implies shared operation, but no page reviewed states which policy or change rights the customer retains. Graded partial rather than yes for that reason.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked nttglobal.net SD-WAN service page, the SD-WAN Service Portfolio Platform page, the nttglobal.net home page and security page, NTT DATA Managed Network Services (both nttdata.com and services.global.ntt), and the NTT DATA/Cisco managed SASE brochure. None mentions tenant isolation, delegated administration, branded/white-label portals or MSP reseller templates. NTT presents itself as the MSP rather than as a platform for other MSPs.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: NTT DATA delivers end-to-end managed SASE services that span consulting, design, build, management, decommissioning and refresh.
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Structured design and migration services are clearly offered across a consult/design/build lifecycle, and the nttglobal.net SD-WAN page states NTT is able to strategically assist organizations with their network transformation and SD-WAN initiatives. The granular items in the definition (pilots, staging, migration runbooks, rollback plans, training) are not itemised on any page reviewed, hence medium confidence.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: NTT's Infrastructure Management Services provide full life cycle: architecture, design, implementation, upgrades, and full proactive 24×7 management of a customer's global network and security infrastructure.
f07_lifecycle_management.note: Quote uses a multiplication sign in 24×7 as printed on the page. Upgrades and full lifecycle management are stated as part of the service. The NTT DATA/Cisco SASE brochure adds decommissioning and refresh to the same lifecycle. Hardware replacement and end-of-life planning are not named in those exact terms.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Unrivaled performance and connectivity options: MPLS, Ethernet, Local Internet, Broadband, LTE/4G in over 190 countries.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: LTE/4G is named as a supported transport option alongside MPLS, Ethernet, internet and broadband. 5G is not named on the SD-WAN service page, the platform page or the security page, and no page reviewed mentions SIM management or signal monitoring. NTT DATA does market a separate Private 5G service, but that is a private cellular network offering rather than evidence of 5G WAN transport in the SD-WAN service, so it is not used to lift this grade.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: Secure Web Gateways located at 75+ globally distributed Local Cloud Centers (LCCs) closer to client locations to protect customers from Internet threats.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: The Local Cloud Centers are NTT's own distributed infrastructure delivering secure web gateway enforcement as a cloud service, which meets the definition of vendor-operated shared gateways. Separately the page describes optimised connectivity to AWS, Azure and Oracle Cloud, but per the definition that cloud onramp capability is not counted as evidence here. The security functions enforced at these gateways may use partner technology, which is graded separately under sse_layer_ownership.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The 75+ Local Cloud Centers are described as globally distributed shared infrastructure with no statement that they can be supplied as customer-hosted, dedicated or sovereign instances. Checked the nttglobal.net SD-WAN service and platform pages, the security page, NTT Global Network Services, NTT DATA Managed Network Services and the NTT DATA/Cisco managed SASE brochure. Absence of a statement is not evidence that the capability is absent.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Our dual-stack Tier-1 Global IP Network spans the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania on a single autonomous system number (AS2914).
f21_private_global_backbone.note: NTT owns and operates a Tier 1 global IP backbone under AS2914 spanning four continents, and publishes contractual inter-region latency, loss and jitter figures for it, which is the strongest form of evidence for this field. Caveat: this is the Global IP Network transit product; none of the SD-WAN or SASE pages reviewed states that SD-WAN inter-region traffic is carried on AS2914 by default rather than over the public internet.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: The Global IP Network Backbone will be available to the customer free of Network Outages 100% of the time.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: NTT publishes a contractual SLA for its Global IP Network covering availability, region-by-region latency, packet loss (average monthly not exceeding 0.1%) and jitter. Confidence is medium because this SLA document covers the IP backbone product; no published SLA percentage or response and change-handling commitment specific to the managed SD-WAN or managed SASE service was located on the pages reviewed.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Built on Cisco's enterprise-grade cloud-native Secure Access technology and powered by NTT DATA's global managed services and AI-driven platform
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Graded partner_integrated because NTT's named SASE offerings are built on other vendors' security technology: Cisco Secure Access (providing FWaaS and DNS security) in the NTT DATA/Cisco brochure, and Palo Alto Networks Prisma SASE in the 2023 Managed Campus Networks announcement. NTT's own SD-WAN portfolio page does describe a Firewall offering with application aware controls and an Intrusion Protection add-on covering protocol anomaly detection, port scan blocking and virus, spyware and bot blocking, but the same page states NTT SD-WAN services support 10+ third-party SD-WAN CPE vendors, so the enforcement engine is another company's technology that NTT operates.

f33_data_loss_prevention.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The nttglobal.net SD Security page lists URL Filtering, Malware Detection, Direct Internet Access, Remote Access, Firewall and App Acceleration but not DLP. The NTT DATA/Cisco managed SASE brochure does not mention data loss prevention. No content classification, blocking, alerting or exception workflow description was found on the SD-WAN service page, platform page, or NTT DATA Managed Network Services pages. The underlying partner platforms (Palo Alto Prisma, Cisco Secure Access) include DLP, but no NTT page reviewed claims it, so this is left unknown rather than inferred.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: NTT's SD-WAN Services are managed by world-class Global Operations Centers that perform 24×7 predictive modeling, monitoring and management
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: Quote uses a multiplication sign in 24×7 as printed on the page. NTT states 24x7 proactive monitoring and management from Global Operations Centers acting as a single point of contact, and the NTT DATA/Cisco brochure states that its ISO-certified operations and ITIL-aligned processes ensure service excellence in all areas, which implies formal change governance. Confidence is medium because no page reviewed explicitly commits to owning incidents through to root cause analysis or to structured periodic service reviews; NTT DATA's SPEKTRA platform page references AI-based root cause analysis as a platform feature but that wording was not independently verified as a contractual service commitment.

delivery_model.quote: Customers have the option to self-manage via a web portal or NTT can offer managed services.
delivery_model.note: NTT DATA / NTT Ltd. is primarily a managed provider: it operates managed SD-WAN, managed SASE and managed network services on third-party CPE and security technology. It is graded both rather than managed_provider only because it also authors and operates its own assets: the NTT SD-WAN platform and NTTView customer portal, the 75+ Local Cloud Centers, the SPEKTRA operations platform, and the Tier 1 AS2914 Global IP Network. It does not author the SASE security stack.

underlay_ownership.quote: Our dual-stack Tier-1 Global IP Network spans the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania on a single autonomous system number (AS2914).
underlay_ownership.note: Mixed. NTT genuinely owns core routing and a Tier 1 global IP backbone under AS2914, for which it publishes contractual latency and loss figures, so it is not a pure reseller. However its SD-WAN service offers MPLS, Ethernet, Local Internet, Broadband and LTE/4G access in over 190 countries, a footprint no single carrier owns, so last-mile access is necessarily sourced from third-party carriers in most markets. No page reviewed states explicitly which access circuits NTT owns versus procures, hence medium confidence.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Built on Cisco's enterprise-grade cloud-native Secure Access technology and powered by NTT DATA's global managed services and AI-driven platform
sse_layer_ownership.note: Partner. Named vendors: Cisco (Cisco Secure Access underpins NTT DATA's Managed SASE per the co-branded brochure) and Palo Alto Networks (Prisma SASE underpins NTT's Managed Campus Networks SASE offering per the February 2023 announcement; Cortex XSIAM underpins its MXDR service per the October 2024 announcement). NTT DATA's group page further states it works with 40+ partners across 60+ technologies including Zscaler and Fortinet. NTT contributes the managed service wrapper, the operations platform and its own Local Cloud Centers, but the SSE enforcement stack is other vendors' technology. Note that the two SASE offerings run on different vendors' technology, recorded in conflicts.

regulatory_documentation.quote: ISO/IEC 27001 is an international standard for Information Security Management Systems (ISMS), providing a structured framework of processes and controls to safeguard the confidentiality, integrity, availability and authenticity of information assets against various threats.
regulatory_documentation.note: Frameworks found and named on NTT's compliance page: ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 50001, PCI DSS, ISAE 3402/SOC 1, ISAE 3000/SOC 2, HIPAA Security Rule, NIST 800-53 High, TISAX, EN 50600, ANSI/TIA-942, OSPAR and Indonesia POJK. Frameworks explicitly NOT found: NHS DSPT, DORA and NIS2 do not appear anywhere on that page. Important scope caveat: these attestations are published for NTT Global Data Centers and the page states certain certifications apply only to specific data centre buildings, so they are not directly scoped to the SD-WAN or managed SASE service. The only service-level statement located is the NTT DATA/Cisco brochure line that its ISO-certified operations and ITIL-aligned processes ensure service excellence in all areas, which names no certificate number or scope and would on its own be assurance_only. Confidence is medium for that reason.

pop_count.quote: Secure Web Gateways located at 75+ globally distributed Local Cloud Centers (LCCs) closer to client locations to protect customers from Internet threats.
pop_count.note: The published figure is 75+ Local Cloud Centers, which is NTT Global Networks' term for its distributed cloud security PoPs. This is the only PoP-style count found. It should not be confused with the separate 190+ countries and territories coverage figure on NTT DATA's Global Network Services page, which describes reach rather than PoPs, nor with the AS2914 backbone footprint, for which no PoP count was published on the pages reviewed.

sla_availability_pct.quote: The Global IP Network Backbone will be available to the customer free of Network Outages 100% of the time.
sla_availability_pct.note: 100% is the published availability commitment for NTT's Global IP Network Backbone (AS2914), accompanied by contractual latency figures per region (50ms Intra US, 80ms Trans-Atlantic, 130ms Trans-Pacific, 285ms Asia to Europe, 95ms Intra Asia, 35ms Intra Europe), average monthly packet loss not exceeding 0.1%, and jitter commitments. Caveat: this percentage is for the IP transit backbone product. No availability percentage specific to the managed SD-WAN or managed SASE service was found on any NTT page reviewed, so this figure should not be read as the SD-WAN service SLA.

sectors.healthcare.quote: Drive positive health outcomes through a connected healthcare ecosystem
sectors.healthcare.note: Graded on a dedicated supplier healthcare industry page carrying named health clients (University Hospitals of Leicester, Independent Health). Important caveat for a SASE and SD-WAN comparison: that page contains no SD-WAN or SASE reference at all, and the only connectivity service named on it is Private 5G. The one healthcare case study found on the supplier site (PSG Group, evidence 28) is an electronic health record integration, not a network engagement. No healthcare SD-WAN or SASE customer was found.

sectors.financial_services.quote: a leading Asian bank in Indonesia
sectors.financial_services.note: Two independent supplier sources. The newsroom item (evidence 15) is SD-WAN specific but the bank is not named. The dedicated Banking and Financial Services industry page (evidence 9) names BBVA and states 320+ clients in this sector globally and 8 of top 15 global banks have been clients, but carries no networking content. Insurance also has its own industry page in the supplier's industry index.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.quote: The Pick n Pay Group is a leading retail company in South Africa, with more than 1,200 stores.
sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: Strongest sector evidence found. A named retail customer with a published managed SD-WAN case study, quantified outcome, and a stated technology stack. The supplier also runs a dedicated Retail and Consumer Packaged Goods industry page (evidence 14) and features Pick n Pay on its global enterprise networking page (evidence 5).

sectors.manufacturing.quote: As a global manufacturer of fiber optic and radio frequency products, HUBER+SUHNER understands the power of connectivity.
sectors.manufacturing.note: Named manufacturer with a published managed SD-WAN case study. Corroborated by the supplier's network case study index (evidence 19), which is dominated by manufacturers and industrials including NXP Semiconductors, Honda Motor Co., Hitachi, Inteva Products and Asahi Glass, several tagged to NTT Global Network Services or Software-Defined Network Service. A dedicated Manufacturing industry page also exists in the industry index.

sectors.energy_utilities.note: Graded yes solely because a dedicated supplier industry page exists, which the grading rubric accepts. This is the thinnest of the sector grades: the page names no customer (the only case study reference is an anonymised Major energy sector organization), and it contains no SD-WAN, SASE or WAN content. Its single network reference is about digitising transmission and distribution grids using IoT and analytics, which is a different thing from enterprise WAN. Treat as corporate-level sector presence, not demonstrated SD-WAN or SASE delivery.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: Streamline operations and deliver exceptional citizen and student experiences
sectors.government_public_sector.note: Dedicated Public Sector and Education industry page naming three public bodies: The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) in the UK, the Virginia Information Technologies Agency and the City of Brownsville in the US. The page lists Global Cellular Connectivity, Enterprise Internet Services and Global IP Network as service links but does not mention SD-WAN or SASE. No published government security accreditation for the network services was found in the pages read.

sectors.education.note: Dedicated Education and Research industry page with one named university client, plus a network services section headed Stay ahead with future-ready, robust networks. Education also appears in the combined Public Sector and Education page (evidence 11). No SD-WAN or SASE named customer in education was found.

sectors.transport_logistics.note: Dedicated Travel, Transportation and Logistics industry page naming Deutsche Bahn, Public Transport Victoria, Trinity Industries, City of Las Vegas and Hilton. The named engagements read as SAP and application work; no SD-WAN or enterprise networking content appears on this page.

sectors.professional_services.quote: Stephenson Harwood is a full service international law firm, with over 120 partners and 700 staff worldwide.
sectors.professional_services.note: A named professional services customer with a published managed network case study covering the firm's entire global network across seven offices in Europe and Asia. Two weaknesses: the engagement is a fully-managed MPLS network rolled out in Q1, 2010, not SD-WAN or SASE, and there is no dedicated professional services industry page in the supplier's industry index (the nearest entries are Private Equity and Telco, Media and Technology).

sectors.hospitality_leisure.quote: Hilton Hotels & Resorts is one of the world's largest and fastest-growing hospitality companies
sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: Graded on a single named case study. The Hilton engagement is website, mobile API and test automation modernisation with no network, SD-WAN or SASE element whatsoever. There is no dedicated hospitality industry page; Hilton is filed under Travel, Transportation and Logistics (evidence 13). A second hospitality client story (Sunburst Hospitality) was seen in search results but not read. Buyers should read this as brand-level sector presence only, not SD-WAN or SASE capability.

regions.uk_ireland.quote: was rolled out in Q1, 2010 and was chosen by Stephenson Harwood to provide its entire global network
regions.uk_ireland.note: UK delivery is evidenced by named UK customers rather than by any published UK coverage statement: a UK law firm's global managed network (evidence 4), The Crown Prosecution Service (evidence 11), University Hospitals of Leicester (evidence 8) and City, University of London. The supplier's en-gb network services path (evidence 32) serves identical global content with no UK-specific coverage claim. No Ireland-specific evidence of any kind was found, so this grade rests entirely on the UK half of the region.

regions.europe.quote: North and South America, Europe, Asia and Australia all connect across a single backbone
regions.europe.note: Backbone-level coverage published by the supplier's own Global IP Network, plus two European delivery instances: SD-WAN terminating at HUBER+SUHNER's Swiss headquarters (evidence 3) and a managed network across seven offices in Europe and Asia (evidence 4). Mondi and BMW Group also appear as European clients on the enterprise networking page (evidence 5), though those case studies were not read.

regions.north_america.quote: North and South America, Europe, Asia and Australia all connect across a single backbone
regions.north_america.note: Continent-level backbone claim plus a US-facing enterprise networking page (evidence 26) describing a Tier 1 IP backbone spanning five continents, and named US public sector clients (Virginia Information Technologies Agency, City of Brownsville) on evidence 11. No North America specific point of presence list or country coverage page was published on any page read; the 190+ country claim is global and undifferentiated.

regions.asia_pacific.quote: IDC MarketScape: Asia/Pacific Managed SD-WAN/SASE Services 2024-2025
regions.asia_pacific.note: The supplier cites a region-specific analyst assessment for managed SD-WAN and SASE in Asia Pacific (evidence 5), and publishes a region-specific SD-WAN engagement for a bank in Indonesia with 120+ branches (evidence 15). Further APAC delivery is implied by the Hong Kong connection point used for the HUBER+SUHNER SD-WAN (evidence 3) and by an APAC regional structure. Note this is the supplier citing an analyst title, not the analyst report itself, which was not accessible.

regions.middle_east_africa.quote: The Pick n Pay Group is a leading retail company in South Africa, with more than 1,200 stores.
regions.middle_east_africa.note: Evidenced for Africa specifically, and strongly so: a managed SD-WAN delivered across more than 1,200 South African stores with loadshedding-resilient satellite failover, and the customer's footprint spanning Botswana, Lesotho, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Swaziland and Zambia. The Middle East half of this region has no evidence at all beyond an undifferentiated global country count and a regional office; do not read this grade as Middle East coverage.

regions.latin_america.quote: North and South America, Europe, Asia and Australia all connect across a single backbone
regions.latin_america.note: Only the continent-level backbone statement supports Latin America, and it names South America rather than Latin America and refers to IP transit infrastructure rather than SD-WAN or SASE service availability. Searches for Latin America specific SD-WAN or managed network coverage returned nothing from the supplier. The supplier does structure a region it calls IBIOL (Iberia, International Organizations, Latin America) with a Madrid headquarters (evidence 27), but that is an office, not published service delivery, so it was not used to grade.

regions.china_mainland.quote: Their first and most pressing requirement was ensuring seamless connectivity between their operations in China and their Swiss headquarters.
regions.china_mainland.note: This is the rare case where a supplier publishes a China-specific SD-WAN outcome rather than a generic global claim, and the case study is titled around linking the customer in China to the rest of the world. Important architectural caveat stated by the supplier itself: delivery was achieved By establishing a single point of connection in Hong Kong, we were able to deliver full SD-WAN capabilities. No page read discloses a mainland Chinese licence, ICP or domestic carrier partnership, so the mechanism for in-country mainland delivery is not published.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: NTT SD-WAN Service Portfolio offers enterprise customers solutions designed to support their global network requirements
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Unambiguous and consistent across every product page read. Reinforced by the customer roster (Honda, Hitachi, Mitsui, BMW Group, Pick n Pay at 1,200+ stores, HUBER+SUHNER across 80+ countries) and by scale language on the managed network services page: over 10K enterprise networks installed and 4.7K+ network engineers in 70+ countries. Every named SD-WAN customer found is a large multinational.

organisation_fit.mid_market.quote: Scalable, world-class IT services tailored for the Mid-Market
organisation_fit.mid_market.note: The group explicitly targets mid-market and claims over 3,000 mid-market clients worldwide, but this sits on an NTT DATA Business Solutions page covering SAP and IT services, and that page does not mention SD-WAN, SASE, network or connectivity anywhere. No mid-market tier, packaged offer or entry point was found for the SD-WAN or SASE portfolio itself. Graded partial rather than yes because the targeting is real at group level but unevidenced for the product in scope.

organisation_fit.small_business.quote: offers enterprise customers solutions designed to support their global network requirements
organisation_fit.small_business.note: No evidence found either way. Checked the SD-WAN portfolio page, the SD-WAN platform page, the campaign microsite, both global and US enterprise networking pages and the managed network services page: all use enterprise, enterprises and global exclusively, with no SMB, small business, small or branch-only tier, and no self-serve or entry-level offer. Absence of small business language is not the same as the supplier saying it does not serve them, so this is unknown rather than not_primary.

published_pricing.note: No price is published that we could quote. The value_tier field on this record is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim.

conflicts.claim_a: NTT's managed SASE offering is built on Palo Alto Networks Prisma SASE, announced 2 February 2023 as a comprehensive managed SASE solution including SD-WAN and cloud-delivered security.
conflicts.claim_b: NTT DATA's managed SASE is built on Cisco's enterprise-grade cloud-native Secure Access technology, providing FWaaS and DNS security.

conflicts.claim_a: Secure Web Gateways located at 75+ globally distributed Local Cloud Centers (LCCs) closer to client locations to protect customers from Internet threats.
conflicts.claim_b: 190+ countries and territories covered by Global Network Services, with no PoP or gateway count published on that page.
